data.title: Winamp Group: Bridger Partners With Groover to Offer Copyright Royalty Collection to the Music Promotion Platform’s Artists
data.description:
Winamp Group: Bridger Partners With Groover to Offer Copyright Royalty Collection to the Music Promotion Platform’s Artists

Groover, a music promotion platform, reports more than 900,000 artists and labels · A further step in the execution of Bridger’s roadmap · A new acquisition channel for Bridger and Winamp for Artists

Regulatory News:

Winamp Group SA (Euronext Growth Paris and Brussels: ALWIN) announces a partnership between Bridger, its copyright management company, and Groover, the platform that connects independent artists with curators, media outlets, radio stations and labels.

The issue is a familiar one. Independent artists rely on a distributor to collect revenue from their recordings, yet the copyright royalties their songs generate, mechanical and performance royalties, often go unclaimed. The partnership brings together two complementary areas of expertise: Groover helps artists get their music in front of curators, media and radio, while Bridger collects the copyright royalties generated every time that music is streamed or broadcast.

A frictionless offer for Groover artists

Through a dedicated page, Groover artists can entrust Bridger with collecting their copyright royalties across more than 80 digital platforms, as well as from radio, television, live performances and public venues in more than 50 countries. Signing up is free and takes just a few minutes. Artists can claim up to 18 months of unpaid royalties and keep around 90% of the amounts collected.

A new acquisition channel for the Group

Groover artists are already investing in promoting their music, which makes them a close match for the established, career-focused projects the Group is prioritising. The partnership is part of the roadmap presented on 5 November, which continues to be rolled out: growing artist acquisition through partners that already work with artists every day.

Since 5 November, Bridger and Winamp have shared the same platform. An artist who joins Bridger for copyright collection can therefore move straight on to the other services offered by Winamp for Artists: distribution, licensing, website building, Fanzone and merchandising.

“For independent artists, getting heard and getting paid are part of the same fight. Groover helps them find their audience, and Bridger makes sure they receive the royalties they are owed. This partnership opens the door to a very large community of artists who are already investing in their careers, and each of them will then be able to discover everything Winamp for Artists has to offer.”
Alexandre Saboundjian, CEO, Winamp Group

NEXT EVENT
31 January 2027 – 2026 revenue release

ABOUT WINAMP GROUP
Based in Brussels and listed on Euronext Growth Paris and Brussels (ALWIN), Winamp Group is building an ecosystem of services for independent artists and their fans. The Group brings together Winamp, Bridger, Jamendo and Hotmix, and offers music distribution, rights management, licensing, promotion and monetisation solutions.

ABOUT BRIDGER – WWW.BRIDGERMUSIC.IO
An independent copyright management entity based in Luxembourg and a CISAC client Rights Management Entity, Bridger enables songwriters and composers to register their works and collect their royalties internationally, through a network of agreements with collective management organisations.

ABOUT GROOVER – WWW.GROOVER.CO
Founded in Paris in 2018, Groover is a music promotion platform that lets independent artists send their tracks to the curators, playlist editors, media outlets, radio stations and labels of their choice, with guaranteed feedback. It reports more than 900,000 artists and labels and over 3,500 curators and music professionals.

This press release contains forward-looking statements based on the Group’s current expectations. They are subject to risks and uncertainties, and actual results may differ materially.

data.title: Japan Tobacco to Book $8.6 Billion Loss on Russia Business
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

Japan Tobacco expects to book an $8.6 billion loss after losing control of its Russian business.

The Japanese tobacco maker said Thursday that it can no longer make business decisions concerning its operations in Russia in the same manner as before.

Earlier this month, Japan Tobacco said all seven of its Russian entities had been placed under temporary administration by a Russian company on the orders of President Vladimir Putin.

The move marked an escalation in Russian measures against Japanese businesses following Tokyo's support for Ukraine and its participation in Western sanctions against Moscow over its 2022 invasion.

Japan Tobacco on Thursday projected a net loss of Y724.00 billion, equivalent to $4.54 billion, for 2026, primarily due to a special loss of Y1.377 trillion related to the loss of control of its Russian business.

The company's Russian operations had about Y1.5 trillion in assets, including goodwill and roughly Y360 billion in cash and deposits, as well as about Y200 billion in liabilities at the end of September, the company said.

Japan Tobacco had expected Russia to account for about 10% of its revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit in 2026.

The Japanese company was previously a state-owned monopoly, but the government held just under 38% of its shares at the end of 2025.

Japan Tobacco, whose brands include Winston and Camel, is one of Russia's largest tobacco companies, with a market share of nearly 40%.

data.title: Evotec and Bristol Myers Squibb Advance Strategic Protein Degradation Partnership with Second IND Acceptance
data.description:
Evotec and Bristol Myers Squibb Advance Strategic Protein Degradation Partnership with Second IND Acceptance

Evotec and Bristol Myers Squibb Advance Strategic Protein Degradation Partnership with Second IND Acceptance

PR Newswire

HAMBURG, Germany, Nov. 19, 2026
  • FDA clearance expands partnered molecular glue pipeline
  • Achievement underscores productivity of the collaboration in molecular glue discovery and potential to address patient populations with high unmet need

HAMBURG, Germany, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evotec SE (NASDAQ: EVO) (Frankfurt Prime Standard: EVT) today announced that its strategic protein degradation partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb has received a second Investigational New Drug (IND) acceptance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The first candidate produced under the partnership entered a Phase 1 clinical trial in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma in March 2026. The second accepted investigational drug candidate, a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD), is expected to enter a Phase 1 clinical trial in 2027.

Initiated in 2018, the partnership combines Evotec's high-performance multi-omics screening, AI-supported data analytics, and drug design capabilities with Bristol Myers Squibb's industry-leading CELMoD agent library. This collaboration, expanded in 2022, continues to advance a pipeline of novel molecular glue degraders for high-value targets in oncology and beyond, translating scientific innovation into a growing therapeutic pipeline.

Dr. Joanna Holbrook, Chief Scientific Officer of Evotec, commented:

"The progression of a second molecular glue candidate to IND acceptance demonstrates the repeatability and productivity of our discovery platform. We are systematically translating complex biology into development candidates. This achievement reinforces the value of our longstanding collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb and further strengthens our confidence in the platform's potential to generate a growing pipeline of investigational drug candidates aimed at addressing substantial unmet medical needs."

About molecular glue degraders

Conventional small molecule therapeutics act through drug-induced interference with protein activity. This limitation to agonistic or antagonistic functions renders about 90% of proteins 'undruggable'. Also, conventional small molecules only work while they are actively binding to the receptor, which typically requires a treatment regimen consisting of one or even several carefully dosed medications every day.

Molecular glue degraders are compounds that induce interactions between an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a molecular target. The induced interaction results in ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of the recruited protein. By inducing neomorphic interactions between CRBN and substrate proteins, CELMoDs enable pharmacological modulation of proteins that may not be amenable to traditional inhibitor or agonist approaches, thereby expanding the potentially druggable proteome.

About Evotec's strategic collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb in molecular glues

In 2018, Evotec entered a long-term strategic drug discovery and development collaboration in the field of molecular glues with Celgene, now Bristol Myers Squibb. Bristol Myers Squibb is a leader in this field based on its unique library of CELMoD agents. The collaboration aims to discover and develop a leading pipeline of molecular glue degraders for a range of therapeutic indications leveraging all of Evotec's proprietary PanOmics and PanHunter platforms as well as AI/ML-based drug discovery and development capabilities.

Evotec applies high-end proteomics and transcriptomics at industrial scale to profile and select promising drug candidates based on comprehensive cell biological profiles. Evotec's leading PanOmics screening capabilities are delivering unmatched throughput. The selection of the most promising candidates for drug development is facilitated by Evotec's PanOmics data analysis platform PanHunter. By integrating and analyzing these data sets, PanHunter supports the identification and advancement of the most promising CELMoDs into lead optimization.

About Evotec SE

Evotec is a life science company pioneering the future of drug discovery and development. By integrating breakthrough science with AI-driven innovation and advanced technologies, Evotec accelerates the journey from concept to cure with greater speed, intelligence and precision. The company's expertise spans small molecules, biologics, cell therapies and associated modalities, supported by proprietary platforms including Molecular Patient Databases, PanOmics and induced pluripotent stem cell-based disease modeling. Through flexible partnering models tailored to customers' needs, Evotec works with all Top 20 pharmaceutical companies, more than 800 biotechnology companies, academic institutions and other healthcare stakeholders. Evotec's offerings range from standalone services to fully integrated research and development programs and long-term strategic partnerships, combining scientific excellence with operational agility. Through Just - Evotec Biologics, the company is redefining biologics development and manufacturing to improve accessibility and affordability. With a portfolio of more than 100 proprietary research and development assets, most of which are co-owned, Evotec focuses on key therapeutic areas including oncology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurology and immunology. Evotec's global team of around 4,500 experts operates from sites in Europe and the United States, providing complementary technologies and services through a network of synergistic centers of excellence. Learn more at www.evotec.com and follow Evotec on LinkedIn and X at @Evotec.

data.title: Sanofi Gets U.S. Approval for Rare Disease Drug
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Sanofi received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for a new drug for a rare inherited disorder called Gaucher disease, the first treatment for neurological symptoms caused by the condition.

The French drugmaker said late Wednesday that its medicine, marketed under the Infilbray brand and also known as venglustat, was authorized in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kilograms--or 33 pounds--for type 3 Gaucher disease, one of the three major forms of the disease.

The FDA said type 3 Gaucher disease affects the brain and nervous system as harmful substances build up in the brain, causing difficulties with coordination, speech and thinking that can worsen over time.

Sanofi said Infilbray is a once-daily oral medicine designed to act across the blood-brain barrier, targeting the abnormal accumulation of fatty substances called glycosphingolipids.

A late-stage clinical trial showed the drug led to significant improvements in certain neurological manifestations of the disease like cognitive deficits and difficulty with coordination and balance, the company said.

Sanofi said Infilbray carries warnings and precautions for suicidal ideation and behavior, clouding of vision in younger patients, and adverse effects on fetal development during pregnancy.

data.title: Treasury Yields Fall in Asian Trade, Shrug off Fed Rate Hike Prospect
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields fall in Asian trade on Thursday, even as the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a fast pace.

Minutes of the latest Fed rate-setting meeting, where the Fed left interest rates unchanged, indicated that some policymakers are leaning toward a larger-than-usual increase of half a percentage point in December. The committee's discussion of inflation revealed increasing concern of broadening price pressure amid strong growth in economic activity, Stuart Paul, U.S. economist at UBS, said in a note.

The minutes pushed higher market expectations of a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike on the Dec. 9 meeting. Money markets currently price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and an 8% likelihood of a 50-basis-point tightening, according to LSEG. A 50-basis-point high was priced with a 2% probability on Wednesday.

"Strong data since the meeting is likely to have strengthened the case for further tightening and we see it as likely that members will indicate another rate increase in their projections in December," Elisabet Kopelman, U.S. economist and Fed watcher at SEB said. "We stick to our view of one more rate increase in December but risks are clearly skewed for another increase, possibly in March," she said.

The two-year Treasury yield slipped 0.4 basis points to 4.795%, while the 10-year Treasury yield declined also 0.4 basis point to 5.061%, according to Tradeweb.

The Treasury will conduct a $19 billion auction of 10-year Treasury inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, on Thursday.

Despite the backdrop of higher real yields, cheap valuations, and improving liquidity, J.P. Morgan analysts think the hawkish Fed backdrop and amount of supply in the 10-year sector means the auction "will need more of a concession to be digested smoothly."

data.title: South Korean Tourism Stocks Rally on Hopes for Expanded China Trade Pact
data.description:
By Kwanwoo Jun

South Korean tourism stocks rallied Thursday on hopes that an expanded free-trade agreement between Seoul and Beijing would boost Chinese visitor arrivals.

China and South Korea earlier this week reached a deal to broaden the scope of their 2015 FTA to include sectors such as tourism, entertainment and investment services, wrapping up years of negotiations, according to President Lee Jae Myung's office in Seoul.

The deal, announced Wednesday after a bilateral summit between Lee and his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, allows South Korean travel agencies to organize outbound travel from 23 regions in China, according to South Korea's trade ministry.

In Seoul trading Thursday, travel company Hanatour Service jumped as much as 28%, while budget airline Jeju Air climbed up to 25%. Hotel Shilla, which operates hotels and duty-free shops, rose as much as 13%.

"The expansion of channels to attract Chinese tourists to South Korea is expected to further boost passenger demand on China routes," Hanwha Investment & Securities analyst Park Su-young said after the deal was reached.

The aviation, entertainment and leisure industries stand to gain from the latest Korea-China pact, with aviation likely to be the biggest beneficiary, she wrote in a research note.

Hana Securities analyst Dohyun Ahn viewed Jeju Air as a key beneficiary of the expanded FTA, citing the company's greater exposure to the Chinese market than any other South Korean low-cost carrier.

Routes to mainland China account for 8% of the South Korean budget airline's revenue, and that share could increase further, Ahn said.

In a statement on Wednesday's expanded deal, President Lee's office said South Korea and China should continue immigration measures to facilitate travel between the two countries to help boost bilateral people-to-people exchanges.

The office expects the number of people traveling between the two countries to reach 10 million this year and hopes it will eventually return to the 13 million recorded in 2016.

Exchanges have been constrained since Beijing allegedly restricted Chinese group tours to South Korea following Seoul's decision in 2016 to deploy a U.S. missile-defense system despite Chinese protests. Beijing has denied imposing a ban.

data.title: Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Novartis forecast steady sales growth through 2031, citing momentum from drugs already in the market and upcoming launches, and said medicines it has in the pipeline would help it sustain growth over the long term.

The Swiss drugmaker said Thursday that it expects annual sales growth of 5% from 2026 to 2031, excluding the effect of currency movements. It had previously forecast annual sales growth in the 5% to 6% range over the 2025-30 period.

Novartis raised its peak sales estimates for key drugs Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio, saying this reinforces confidence in the company's midterm outlook.

The company said it now has nine in-market products with potential to generate annual peak sales of between $3 billion and $10 billion, as well as 10 in late-stage development that could bring in multibillion-dollar sales at their peak.

Novartis also said it is on track to return to a core operating profit margin above 40% by 2029, as previously indicated.

data.title: KKR Invests in India Renewables Business Run by Petronas-Backed Gentari
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Investment firm KKR has made a minority investment in a renewable-energy platform in India run by Gentari, an entity established by Malaysia's national oil and gas company.

The investment will provide growth capital to support the renewables platform's continued expansion in India, KKR and Gentari said Thursday.

No terms were disclosed.

KKR has been investing in India's infrastructure sector for more than a decade, and has committed more than $27 billion to energy-transition and renewables infrastructure globally since 2011.

The deal with Gentari--part of Petronas Group--aims to capture the need for continued investment in India's energy infrastructure as demand for reliable power grows rapidly.

"We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand," said Hardik Shah, Asia-Pacific infrastructure partner at KKR.

Gentari's India platform has about 8 gigawatts of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable-energy capacity. Its portfolio spans solar, wind, hybrid and battery-energy storage solutions.

Gentari Group Chief Executive Sushil Purohit said that with KKR's support, it is well-positioned to keep scaling the business.

Following the investment, Gentari will retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform, the companies said.

The tie-up comes on the heels of KKR's roughly $16 billion partnership with RWE investing in offshore-wind farms in the U.K.

data.title: Square Australia and NAB Team Up to Make Business Simpler
data.description:
Square Australia and NAB Team Up to Make Business Simpler

Square Australia and National Australia Bank (NAB) are teaming up to make banking and payments simpler for Australian businesses and give them greater control over their cash flow.

For small businesses, including those in retail and hospitality, cash flow matters, margins matter and time matters. The partnership combines NAB’s business banking expertise with Square’s leading payments and business tools to make it easier for customers to manage the everyday work of running a business.

Initially, the partnership will provide eligible NAB customers using Square access to Square’s flexible transfer feature, giving them more control over when their available funds are sent to their NAB Business Transaction Account.

From February next year, businesses can set a close of day time for each day of the week, with Square initiating the transfer of their available funds to their NAB Business Transaction Account 15 minutes later.

NAB Group Executive Business and Private Banking Andrew Auerbach said the partnership reflected the bank’s ambition to keep supporting customers to make running their business easier.

“Many hospitality and retail businesses don’t operate nine to five,” Mr. Auerbach said.

“A restaurant might finish trading late at night and need to pay suppliers the next morning. A café might need to buy tomorrow’s produce, so their banking and payments need to work around how they do business.

“NAB already supports businesses of all shapes and sizes across Australia. We want to keep raising the bar by finding practical ways to make running them easier.

“These sound like small things, but they can make a big difference when you’re running a business. Flexible transfer is the first Square feature being made available through the partnership and we want to build on it.”

Block Global Partnerships Lead Morgan Kuntze said the partnership combined Square’s technology and understanding of sellers with NAB’s expertise in business banking.

“Square works with businesses every day, helping them take payments and manage the day-to-day work that sits behind making a sale,” Ms. Kuntze said.

“By partnering with NAB, we can connect that experience more closely with banking and find new ways to make managing money simpler for sellers.

“Flexible transfer is the first step. Sellers can set their close of day schedule around the way their business operates, and Square automatically initiates the transfer of their available funds.”

For Axil Coffee Roasters, which has grown from a single Hawthorn cafe to more than 16 locations and hundreds of wholesale partners, managing cash flow is part of the everyday reality of running a growing hospitality business.

“There’s no standard working day in hospitality,” said Axil Managing Director David Makin.

“Some of our venues open incredibly early, others trade later, and every day we’re managing staff, stock and suppliers across the business.

“Being able to set our transfer schedule around how we actually trade gives us another level of control over our cash flow.

“We need the flexibility. The more our banking and payments can fit around how the business actually operates, rather than the other way around, the better.”

Through the partnership, NAB and Square plan to build on flexible transfer by exploring further ways to connect banking and payments, simplify cash flow and make it easier for Australian businesses to operate and grow.

NAB has opened up the ability for businesses to express interest in the partnership ahead of the full launch in early 2027 - click here for more information.

Notes to editors:

  • NAB’s current standard settlement time is 9.30pm AEST daily.
  • Square’s flexible transfers require a linked and eligible NAB Business Transaction Account. The availability of funds in the linked bank account may be affected by NAB processing requirements.
  • Square applies transfer limits ranging from $5 to $50,000 AUD per day (new sellers are limited to $5,000 AUD per day until eligible for a higher limit). Flexible Transfers may not be available in limited circumstances beyond Square’s control, including where the linked bank account is not eligible for real-time payments or where there is downtime or delay affecting the New Payments Platform. Square’s Terms of Service apply.

About Square
Square helps businesses turn transactions into connections and businesses into neighbourhood favourites. In 2009, Square started with a simple invention — the first mobile card reader, which changed how the entire financial system thinks about small businesses. Square has since grown into a global business platform helping millions of sellers of all sizes participate and thrive in their communities. Whether independently run or a global chain, Square understands that sellers succeed when they have the freedom to focus on the experiences that keep customers coming back. From point of sale and payments to online commerce, staff management, cash flow tools, and more, Square brings together the tools sellers need to run and grow on one intelligent platform. For more information, visit squareup.com.

About NAB
At National Australia Bank (NAB) Group, our ambition is to be the most customer-centric company in Australia and New Zealand. More than 41,000 colleagues at the bank provide 10 million customers with secure, easy and reliable banking services. About 88% of the Group’s workforce are located in Australia and New Zealand, while others work in Asia, London, New York and Paris. NAB is proud to be Australia’s largest business lender. We stand by our customers, and they have our ongoing support.
